svg.text: Implements architecture-generic.svg on AWS · Compute · DB · Messaging (fan-out) · Monitoring · Scaling
JWT verified again inside each service (defense in depth)
VPC link, path-based → the 3 domain APIs
.NET 8 container · no sync call into Requests
⚠ if the broker is down: publishers (Outbox Relays) keep
retrying locally — an unsent row is never "dead"
sync fallback: resolve recipient if missing
Monitoring & Ops (shared, one stack for all 5 domains)
• 5xx rate / p95 latency (any of the 3 sync APIs)
• RDS CPU / connections (any of the 4 databases)
rationale: these are the DLQs where a stuck consumer blocks work others depend on
Log-only Alarms → reviewed periodically, no page
rationale: nothing else depends on Reporting staying fresh — it drains the
backlog and catches up; paging on-call for it would be alert fatigue
What this diagram fixes vs. the earlier extended-architecture proposal (2-cloud-aws.svg)
1. Documents and Reporting are no longer missing
The earlier diagram only mapped Customers/Requests/Notifications. This one adds Documents (API + store + outbox relay + S3 for
blobs) and Reporting (consumer + its own read-model RDS), matching all 5 domains in architecture-generic.svg.
2. Messaging is fan-out, not a single serial queue
A single SQS queue can only support one logical consumer group. Since Notifications, Reporting and (for DocumentUploaded)
Requests each need an independent subscription per architecture-generic.svg, this uses SNS topics fanning out to one SQS queue
per consumer, each with its own redrive policy — the standard AWS pattern for that requirement.
3. DLQ severity is per-consumer, not one blanket alarm
notifications-dlq and requests-doc-dlq page on-call (their consumers block real work or user-facing status). reporting-dlq is
log-only (nothing depends on Reporting staying fresh) — this mirrors the blast-radius note in architecture-generic.svg exactly.
4. The Requests→Customers and Notifications→Customers sync calls now carry their resilience requirement explicitly
Both are marked ⚠ needing a timeout + circuit breaker + cached/last-known snapshot, since these are the only hard synchronous
dependencies in the system — a Customers outage would otherwise cascade into both callers failing.
Scope: this diagram assumes architecture-generic.svg has been implemented. For the AWS mapping of the code as it exists today, see 3-cloud-aws-current-code.svg.
